newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr's run slows, sterling down on rates fear.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr's run slows, sterling down on rates fear.

text.p: The dollar's powerful run slowed on Tuesday as traders pocketed profits and the British pound was knocked further from recent peaks by talk that British interest rates might not be increased in the near future.

Equity markets got off to a healthy start. Weaker sterling, seen helping British exporters, boosted London's stocks by 0.5 percent and Paris also climbed 0.5 percent to within a whisker of its trading record.
The U.S. currency, which surged to a seven-and-a-half year high of 1.8490 marks at one stage on Monday, shed one-and-a-half pfennigs by midday in Europe to trade at 1.8346 marks.
Dealers said the dollar now needed a kickstart to set off towards new highs again. Positive data or gains in U.S. assets could help it rebound.

"It's been fairly quiet today with the dollar caught below psychological levels at around 1.84 marks," said Kit Juckes, currency strategist at NatWest Markets. "However, the dollar is well underpinned and it is only a matter of time before it starts moving higher and makes new highs against the mark."
A buy signal could come from American employment figures due at 1230 GMT. Confirmation that inflation is under control would bolster U.S. assets and hence the dollar.

"There's still a good chance the dollar can reach 1.85 which would be very bullish technically," said First Chicago economist Teis Knuthsen. "But the market is getting a bit more hesitant and is looking for confirmation of the uptrend."

The dollar, up five percent against the mark in the last three weeks, has also benefited from a growing conviction that Europe's planned single currency would be launched with a broad group of countries, making for a weak euro.
Sterling, which shed five pfennigs against the mark on Monday, was the other key focus for traders, tumbling another two pfennigs to 2.9980 marks by lunch-time.

Some dealers said the pound's plunge from its 25 percent increase over the last year against a trade-weighted basket of currencies looked more like a correction than the first leg of a big sell-off, analysts said.
"Sterling had a fantastic rally, and if you put that into context, yesterday's fall was not quite as dramatic as it looked at first sight," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London.

The downturn was partly prompted by talk that the Bank of England monetary policy committee might hold off another interest rate rise when it meets next week. Complaints from UK exporters have been getting louder about the harmful strength of sterling.

A counter-argument, that an August rate rise was likely, came in figures on Tuesday showing a record rise in personal credit, which suggested British consumers are borrowing heavily as well as spending freely.

"This data tells us just how buoyant consumers are feeling. Not only are they spending their windfall cash, but they are happy to borrow more as well," said James Barty, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"The big headache facing the Bank is how can it slow down the consumer without driving the pound up. We think it will raise rates by a quarter point and hint that it may then pause for a while."

The falling pound, making British exports more competitive, helped the London bourse. The FTSE-100 index was up nearly 0.4 percent at midday, lifted by engineering stocks which bounced in response to the pound's fall sharp fall.
"There's a knee-jerk reaction from the engineers in particular, which have been hit the hardest," one dealer said.
"Sterling has lifted the pressure on these exporting companies but two days doesn't change things given the relentless pressure those companies have been under."
In Frankfurt, stocks climbed to 27.51 points to 4398.67, close to the all-time trading high, before falling back by midday.
Paris stocks, which hit an intra-day high on Monday, were up by 0.5 percent by lunchtime, inching towards record levels helped by gains in the bonds market.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8346 marks and 117.39 yen compared to 1.8466 and 117.70 in late trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index up 16.4 points at 4,878.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 10.61 points in bourse trade at 4,381.69.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 15.66 points at 3,037.86.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $327.50 an ounce, unchanged from Monday's close. Silver was down two cents at $4.37.
